$comment: What production's alembic_version is KNOWN to record, and when that was last verified.
This file exists because promote-to-prod.yml runs on a GitHub-hosted runner with no
route to the production database: it cannot ask. So the guard compares the repo's
alembic head against this declared value instead, and the value is only trustworthy
because updating it is a reviewed commit — see docs/runbooks/ALEMBIC_CONVERGENCE.md.
It is a LEDGER, not a source of truth. The database is the truth; this records the
last time a human read it with `alembic_converge.py --check` from the janua-api pod.
Stale is the expected failure mode, and it fails SAFE: a ledger left behind makes the
guard demand migrations_acknowledged=true on promotes that may not need it, which
costs an operator one checkbox and one look at the database. The opposite — a ledger
edited forward without running the check — defeats the guard entirely, which is why
verified_at and verified_by are required and why the runbook makes reading the
database the step that precedes editing this file.
notes: 012, 013, 015 and 016 were applied BY HAND and never stamped.
014 (capability_links) was applied via generated SQL by the operator's bootstrap,
Convergence has NOT been performed yet: run scripts/alembic_converge.py --stamp,
then set recorded_revision to the value it reports and refresh verified_at.
